title.zh: 卷一百八十八 列傳第七十五: 董摶霄 劉哈剌不花 王英 石抹宜孫
title.en: Volume 188 Biographies 75: Dong Tuanxiao, Liuhalabuhua, Wang Ying, Shimoyisun
title.raw: 卷一百八十八 列傳第七十五: 董摶霄 劉哈剌不花 王英 石抹宜孫 Volume 188 Biographies 75: Dong Tuanxiao, Liuhalabuhua, Wang Ying, Shimoyisun

sentences.zh: 董摶霄弟昂霄

translations.literal: Dong Tuanxiao's younger brother Angxiao
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tuanxiao's Younger Brother Angxiao

sentences.zh: 董摶霄，字孟起，磁州人。

translations.literal: Dong Tuanxiao, courtesy name Mengqi, was a man of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tuanxiao, courtesy name Mengqi, was a native of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 由國子生辟陝西行台掾。

translations.literal: From an Imperial Academy student he was recruited as a clerk of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited from among the Imperial Academy students, he was appointed a clerk of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時天大旱，從侍御史郭貞讞獄華陰縣，有李謀兒累殺商賈於道，為賊十五年，至百餘事。

translations.literal: At the time heaven was greatly drought-stricken. Following Supervising Censor Guo Zhen in trying cases at Huayin County, there was Li Mou'er, who repeatedly killed merchants on the roads, acting as a bandit for fifteen years, amounting to more than a hundred cases.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a severe drought afflicted the land. While accompanying Supervising Censor Guo Zhen in hearing cases at Huayin County, he encountered the case of Li Mou'er, who had spent fifteen years as a highway robber, repeatedly murdering merchants in more than a hundred incidents.

sentences.zh: 事覺，獄已具，賄賂有司，謂徒黨未盡獲，五年不決，人皆以為憤。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light the case was already complete, but he bribed officials, saying his accomplices had not all been captured; for five years no verdict was reached, and people all regarded it with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crime was exposed the case was fully prepared for judgment, yet Li Mou'er bribed the officials, claiming that not all his accomplices had been caught. For five years no verdict was rendered, and public outrage mounted.

sentences.zh: 摶霄知之，以言於貞，即以屍諸市中，天乃大雨。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao learned of this and spoke of it to Zhen; the corpse was immediately displayed in the marketplace, and heaven then sent great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao learned of the situation and reported it to Guo Zhen, who immediately had the corpse displayed in the marketplace. Heaven then sent down torrential rain.

sentences.zh: 授四川肅政廉訪司知事，除涇陽縣尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed clerk of the Sichuan Commission for Purifying Administration and Investigating Censors, and was made magistrate of Jingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk of the Sichuan Commission for Purifying Administration and Investigating Censors, and later served as magistrate of Jingyang County.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部主事，升員外郎，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to vice director, and was appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, promoted to vice director, and appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 又出僉遼東肅政廉訪司事，歷江西行省左右司郎中，遷浙東宣慰副使。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as associate commissioner of the Liaodong Commission for Purifying Administration and Investigating Censors, served as director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and was transferred to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was again dispatched as associate commissioner of the Liaodong Commission for Purifying Administration and Investigating Censors, served as a director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and was later transferred to vice commissioner of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 其歷官所至，往往理冤獄，革弊政，才譽益著稱於時。

translations.literal: Wherever he served in office, he often redressed wrongful cases and reformed corrupt policies; his talent and reputation grew ever more celebrated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he regularly cleared wrongful convictions and abolished corrupt practices, and his talent and reputation steadily grew until he was widely acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，除濟寧路總管，奉旨從江浙平章教化徵進安豐，兵至合肥定林站，遇賊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng he was appointed prefect of Jining Circuit. By imperial order he followed Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat Pingzhang Jiaohua on a campaign toward Anfeng. When the army reached Dinglin Station at Hefei, they encountered bandits and inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng (1351), he was appointed prefect of Jining Circuit. By imperial order he joined Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat Pingzhang Jiaohua on a campaign to relieve Anfeng. When the army reached Dinglin Station near Hefei, it encountered rebel forces and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 時硃皋、固始賊复猖獗，軍少不足以分討。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits at Zhugao and Gushi again grew fierce; the army was too few to divide for separate suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebel activity at Zhugao and Gushi flared up again, and the army was too small to divide for simultaneous operations.

sentences.zh: 有大山民寨及芍陂屯田軍，摶霄皆獎勞而約束之，遂得障蔽硃皋。

translations.literal: There were the Dashan civilian stockade and the Shaopi garrison-farm troops; Tuanxiao rewarded, comforted, and disciplined them all, and thus was able to shield Zhugao.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao rewarded, encouraged, and put under discipline both the Dashan civilian stockade and the Shaopi garrison-farm troops, thereby securing a defensive screen before Zhugao.

sentences.zh: 我軍屯硃家寺，賊至，追殺之。

translations.literal: Our army encamped at Zhujia Temple; when bandits arrived, they were pursued and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Zhujia Temple, and when rebels appeared they were pursued and cut down.

sentences.zh: 乃遣進士程明仲往諭賊中，招徠者千二百家，因悉知其虛實。

translations.literal: He then sent jinshi Cheng Mingzhong to announce terms within the bandit ranks; more than twelve hundred households were recruited, and thereby he came to know their strengths and weaknesses in full.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the jinshi Cheng Mingzhong to proclaim terms among the rebels, winning over more than twelve hundred households and thereby learning their full disposition.

sentences.zh: 夜縛浮橋於淝水，既渡，賊始覺。

translations.literal: By night they lashed a pontoon bridge across the Fei River; only after the crossing did the bandits become aware.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of night they built a pontoon bridge across the Fei River and crossed before the rebels even noticed.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數万據磵南，我軍渡者，輒為其所敗。

translations.literal: Bandit forces numbering tens of thousands held the south of the ravine; our troops who crossed were repeatedly defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels held the south bank of the ravine, and every unit that crossed was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 摶霄乃麾騎士，別渡淺灘襲賊後。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao then commanded the cavalry to cross separately at a shallow ford and strike the bandits from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao then ordered the cavalry to ford at a shallow crossing elsewhere and attack the rebels from behind.

sentences.zh: 賊回東南向，與騎士迎敵，摶霄忽躍馬渡磵，揚言於眾曰：「賊已敗。

translations.literal: The bandits turned southeast to meet the cavalry in battle. Tuanxiao suddenly leapt his horse across the ravine and proclaimed to the host: "The bandits are already defeated."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wheeled southeast to engage the cavalry. Tuanxiao suddenly spurred his horse across the ravine and shouted to the troops: "The enemy is already beaten!"

sentences.zh: 」諸軍皆渡，一鼓而擊之。

translations.literal: "All the armies crossed, and with one drum-roll they struck them.
translations.idiomatic: All the units crossed over and, at a single roll of the drums, charged the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，亟追殺之，相藉以死者二十五里，遂復安豐。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly defeated; he urgently pursued and killed them, and the dead lay piled upon one another for twenty-five li; Anfeng was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suffered a crushing defeat. Tuanxiao pressed the pursuit, and corpses lay stacked along the route for twenty-five li. Anfeng was thus restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年，有旨命摶霄攻濠州，又命移軍援江南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an imperial order commanded Tuanxiao to attack Haozhou, and also ordered him to move his army to aid Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1352), an imperial edict ordered Tuanxiao to attack Haozhou and then to shift his army south to relieve Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 遂渡江，至湖州德清縣，而徽、饒賊已陷杭州。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river and reached Deqing County in Huzhou, while the bandits of Huizhou and Raozhou had already taken Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi and reached Deqing County in Huzhou, only to learn that rebels from Huizhou and Raozhou had already captured Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 教化問摶霄計，摶霄曰：「賊皆野人，見杭城子女玉帛，非平日所有，必縱慾，不暇為備，宜急攻之。

translations.literal: Jiaohua asked Tuanxiao for a plan. Tuanxiao said: "The bandits are all country folk. Seeing Hangzhou's women, children, jade, and silk—things not theirs in ordinary times—they are sure to give free rein to their desires and have no leisure to prepare defenses. We should attack them urgently."
translations.idiomatic: Jiaohua asked Tuanxiao for counsel. Tuanxiao replied: "These rebels are country people. Confronted with Hangzhou's women, children, and riches—luxuries they have never known—they will surely abandon themselves to plunder and neglect their defenses. We should strike at once."

sentences.zh: 今欲退保湖州，設使賊乘銳直趨京口，則江南不可為矣。

translations.literal: If we now wish to withdraw and hold Huzhou, suppose the bandits, riding their momentum, drive straight for Jingkou—then Jiangnan will be beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: If we now fall back to defend Huzhou, and the rebels, emboldened by victory, drive straight for Jingkou, all of Jiangnan will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」教化猶豫未決，而諸將亦難其行。

translations.literal: "Jiaohua hesitated and could not decide, and the generals also found the march difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaohua hesitated, unable to decide, and the other generals balked at the advance.

sentences.zh: 摶霄正色曰：「江浙相君方面既陷於賊，今可取而不取，誰任其咎！

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said with stern countenance: "The Jiang-Zhe regional commander has already lost his territory to bandits. If we can recover it now and do not, who will bear the blame!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao said sternly: "The Jiang-Zhe regional commander has already lost his command to the rebels. If we can retake the city now and fail to do so, who will answer for it?"

sentences.zh: 」复拔劍顧諸將曰：「諸君荷國厚恩，而臨難苟免，今相君在是，敢有慢令者斬。

translations.literal: "He again drew his sword, looked at the generals, and said: "You gentlemen owe the state deep favor, yet at peril you seek only to escape. The regional commander is here now; whoever dares disobey orders shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and turned to the generals: "You have all received great favor from the state, yet in the face of danger you would shirk your duty. The regional commander is present. Anyone who dares defy orders will be executed."

sentences.zh: 」計乃決。

translations.literal: "The plan was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 遂進兵杭城。

translations.literal: He then advanced his army to Hangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: The army then marched on Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊迎敵，至鹽橋，摶霄麾壯士突前，斬殺數級，而諸軍相繼夾擊之，凡七戰，追殺​​至清河坊。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to meet the enemy. At Salt Bridge, Tuanxiao commanded stalwart men to charge forward, beheading several ranks; then the various armies successively attacked from both sides. In all there were seven battles, and the pursuit and killing reached Qinghe Ward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to fight. At Salt Bridge, Tuanxiao sent picked warriors charging ahead and cut down several enemy officers. The other units then closed in from both flanks. After seven engagements the pursuit carried as far as Qinghe Ward.

sentences.zh: 賊奔接待寺，塞其門而焚之，賊皆死，遂復杭州。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to the Reception Temple, blocked its gate, and set it afire; the bandits all died, and Hangzhou was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into the Reception Temple, barricaded the doors, and set the building ablaze, perishing in the flames. Hangzhou was thus restored.

sentences.zh: 已而餘杭、武康、德清次第以平，摶霄亦受代去。

translations.literal: Before long Yuhang, Wukang, and Deqing were pacified in succession, and Tuanxiao also completed his term of office and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuhang, Wukang, and Deqing were pacified in turn, and Tuanxiao completed his tour of duty and departed.

sentences.zh: 徽、饒賊復自昱嶺關寇於潛，行省乃假摶霄為參知政事，俾复提兵討之。

translations.literal: The bandits of Huizhou and Raozhou again raided Yuqian from Yuling Pass. The Branch Secretariat thereupon provisionally appointed Tuanxiao as vice administrator of government affairs and ordered him again to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Huizhou and Raozhou again invaded Yuqian through Yuling Pass. The Branch Secretariat temporarily appointed Tuanxiao vice administrator of government affairs and ordered him to take command once more and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 摶霄曰：「必欲除殘去暴，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said: "If you truly wish to eliminate the cruel and remove the violent, I dare not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao said: "If the task is to destroy the cruel and suppress the violent, I shall not refuse."

sentences.zh: 若假以重爵，則不​​敢受。

translations.literal: If you grant me a heavy rank in pretense, then I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: But if you offer me a lofty title merely for show, I cannot accept it."

sentences.zh: 」即日引兵至臨安新溪，是為入杭要路，既分兵守之而始進兵至叫口及虎檻，遇賊，皆大破之，追殺至於潛，遂復其縣治。

translations.literal: "That same day he led troops to Xinxi in Lin'an—the key route into Hangzhou. After dividing forces to hold it, he then advanced to Jiaokou and Hujian, encountered bandits, and defeated them all greatly. Pursuit and killing reached Yuqian, and its county seat was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he led his troops to Xinxi in Lin'an, the vital approach to Hangzhou. After detaching units to hold that route, he advanced to Jiaokou and Hujian, routed the rebels in both places, pursued them to Yuqian, and restored the county seat.

sentences.zh: 既又克復昌化縣及昱嶺關，降賊將潘大ＣＯ二千人。

translations.literal: He then also recovered Changhua County and Yuling Pass, and the bandit general Pan Da and two thousand men surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He next recovered Changhua County and Yuling Pass, and the rebel general Pan Da surrendered with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賊又有犯千秋關者，摶霄還軍守於潛，而賊兵大至，焚倚郭廬舍。

translations.literal: Bandits again violated Qianqiu Pass. Tuanxiao returned his army to hold Yuqian, while bandit troops arrived in great numbers and burned the outlying dwellings near the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels again threatened Qianqiu Pass. Tuanxiao withdrew to defend Yuqian, where a large enemy force arrived and burned the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 摶霄按軍不動，左右請出兵，摶霄曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao held his army still and did not move. Those at his side asked to send out troops. Tuanxiao said: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao held his army in place. His officers urged him to engage, but he said: "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 」遣人執白旗登山望賊，約曰：「賊以我為怯，必少懈；

translations.literal: "He sent men bearing white flags up the mountain to watch the bandits, with this agreement: "The bandits will think us timid and are sure to relax somewhat;"
translations.idiomatic: He sent men with white flags up the heights to watch the enemy, instructing them: "The rebels will think us timid and let their guard down;"

sentences.zh: 伺其有間，則麾所執旗。

translations.literal: when you see an opening, then wave the flags you hold.
translations.idiomatic: when you see an opening, wave your flags."

sentences.zh: 」又伏兵城外，皆授以火砲，复約曰：「見旗動，砲即發。

translations.literal: "He also hid troops outside the city and gave them all fire-lances, again agreeing: "When you see the flags move, the fire-lances are to be discharged at once."
translations.idiomatic: He also placed ambush troops outside the walls and armed them with fire-lances, with the same signal: "When the flags move, open fire."

sentences.zh: 」已而旗動，砲發，兵乃盡出，斬首數知級，遂復千秋關。

translations.literal: "Before long the flags moved, the fire-lances were discharged, and the troops then all sallied forth. Several thousand heads were cut off, and Qianqiu Pass was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the flags waved, the fire-lances roared, and the whole army surged out, taking several thousand heads. Qianqiu Pass was restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊復攻獨松、百丈、幽嶺三關，摶霄乃先以兵守多溪。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits again attacked the three passes of Dusong, Baizhang, and Youling. Tuanxiao then first sent troops to hold Duoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels again assaulted the three passes at Dusong, Baizhang, and Youling. Tuanxiao first deployed troops to hold Duoxi.

sentences.zh: 多溪，三關要路也。

translations.literal: Duoxi was the vital route of the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Duoxi was the key route linking the three passes.

sentences.zh: 既又分為三軍：一出獨松，一出百丈，一出幽嶺。

translations.literal: He then again divided into three armies: one out from Dusong, one out from Baizhang, one out from Youling.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his force into three columns, one advancing through each pass.

sentences.zh: 然後會兵搗賊巢，遂乘勝復安吉，七戰而克之，賊將以其徒來降者數百人。

translations.literal: Then he united the armies and struck the bandit nest. Riding victory he recovered Anji; in seven battles he took it. Bandit generals came leading their followers to surrender, numbering several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The columns then converged on the rebel stronghold, and riding the momentum they recovered Anji after seven battles. Several hundred rebel officers and their followers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 既數日，賊復來窺獨松。

translations.literal: Several days later the bandits again came to probe Dusong.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the rebels again probed Dusong Pass.

sentences.zh: 摶霄即以兵守苦嶺及黃沙嶺。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao immediately sent troops to hold Kul Ridge and Huangsha Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao immediately posted troops at Kul Ridge and Huangsha Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊帥梅元來降，且言復有帥十一人欲降者，即遣偏將餘思忠至賊寨諭之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Mei Yuan came to surrender, and moreover said that eleven other chiefs also wished to surrender. Tuanxiao immediately sent the deputy general Yu Sizhong to the bandit stockade to announce terms to them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Mei Yuan came over and reported that eleven other chiefs also wished to surrender. Tuanxiao sent Deputy General Yu Sizhong to the rebel camp to accept their submission.

sentences.zh: 賊皆入暗室潛議，思忠持火投入室內，拔劍語眾曰：「元帥命我來活汝，汝復何議！

translations.literal: The bandits all entered a dark room to deliberate in secret. Sizhong held fire and threw it into the room, drew his sword, and said to the crowd: "The commander ordered me to come and spare your lives—what are you still deliberating about!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew into a dark room to confer in secret. Sizhong tossed a torch inside, drew his sword, and shouted: "The commander sent me to spare your lives—what is there left to discuss!"

sentences.zh: 」已而火起，焚其寨，叱賊黨散去，而引賊帥來降。

translations.literal: "Before long fire rose and burned their stockade. He shouted at the bandit partisans to disperse, and led the bandit chiefs to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Flames soon engulfed the camp. He drove the rebel bands away and escorted the rebel chiefs back to surrender.

sentences.zh: 明日，進兵廣德，克之。

translations.literal: The next day he advanced his army to Guangde and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he marched on Guangde and captured it.

sentences.zh: 有蘄賊與饒、池諸賊复犯徽州。

translations.literal: There were bandits from Qi together with bandits from Rao, Chi, and other places who again violated Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Qi, together with forces from Raozhou, Chizhou, and elsewhere, again invaded Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 賊中有道士，能作十二里霧。

translations.literal: Among the bandits was a Daoist priest who could produce a twelve-li fog.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rebels was a Daoist priest who could summon a fog twelve li wide.

sentences.zh: 摶霄以兵擊之，已而妖霧開豁，諸伏兵皆起，襲賊兵後，賊大潰亂，斬首數万級，擒千餘人。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao attacked them with troops. Before long the demonic fog cleared and opened wide; all the hidden troops rose up and struck the bandit army from the rear. The bandits fell into great rout and disorder. Tens of thousands of heads were cut off, and more than a thousand were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao attacked with his army. Soon the sorcerous fog lifted, ambush troops sprang up behind the rebel line, and the enemy collapsed in chaos. Tens of thousands were slain and more than a thousand taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 獲道士，焚其妖書而斬之。

translations.literal: The Daoist priest was captured; his sorcerous books were burned and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the priest, burned his occult texts, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 遂平徽州。

translations.literal: Huizhou was thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou was thus pacified.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除水軍都萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed commander-in-chief of the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1354) he was appointed commander-in-chief of the naval forces.

sentences.zh: 俄升樞密院判官，從丞相脫脫徵高郵，分戍鹽城、興化。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and followed Chancellor Toqtoghan on a campaign against Gaoyou, dividing forces to garrison Yancheng and Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and joined Chancellor Toqtoghan's campaign against Gaoyou, detaching units to garrison Yancheng and Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 賊巢在大縱、德勝兩湖間，凡十有二，悉剿平之。

translations.literal: Bandit nests lay between the two lakes of Dazong and Desheng; in all there were twelve, and all were suppressed and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve rebel strongholds lay between the Dazong and Desheng lakes, and he wiped them all out.

sentences.zh: 即其地築芙蓉寨，賊入，輒迷故道，盡殺之，自是不復敢犯。

translations.literal: On that ground he built Furong Stockade. When bandits entered, they always lost the old paths and were all killed; from then on they no longer dared to violate it.
translations.idiomatic: On that ground he built Furong Stockade. Rebels who entered lost their way and were slaughtered to the last man, and from then on none dared approach.

sentences.zh: 賊恃習水，渡淮北，據安東州。

translations.literal: The bandits, relying on their skill in water, crossed north of the Huai River and seized Andong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in their mastery of water warfare, the rebels crossed north of the Huai and seized Andong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 摶霄招善水戰者五百人，與賊戰安東之大湖，大敗之，遂復安東。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao recruited five hundred men skilled in naval combat and fought the bandits at the Great Lake of Andong, inflicting a great defeat on them, and Andong was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao recruited five hundred skilled naval fighters and met the rebels on the Great Lake at Andong, routing them and recovering the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，剿平北沙、廟灣、沙浦等寨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he suppressed and pacified the stockades of Beisha, Miaowan, Shapu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1356) he suppressed the rebel stockades at Beisha, Miaowan, Shapu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵泗州，不利。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced troops to Sizhou, but the outcome was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: He soon advanced on Sizhou but met with defeat.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝東下，斷我軍糧道，乃回軍屯北沙，糧且絕，與賊死戰，凡七晝夜。

translations.literal: The bandits, riding their victory, pressed eastward and cut our army's supply route. He then returned the army to encamp at Beisha. Provisions were nearly exhausted, and he fought the bandits to the death for seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed their advantage eastward and severed the army's supply lines. Tuanxiao withdrew to Beisha, where provisions ran out and he fought the enemy to the death for seven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 賊敗走，奪賊船七十餘，乃得渡淮，保泗州。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled. More than seventy bandit boats were seized, and only then could they cross the Huai and hold Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled. After seizing more than seventy of their boats, the army crossed the Huai and held Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，湖水溢，諸營皆避去，而摶霄獨守孤城，賊環繞數十里攻之。

translations.literal: At the time it was midsummer rains and the lake waters overflowed. All the camps withdrew, but Tuanxiao alone held the isolated city while bandits encircled it for several tens of li and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer, with heavy rains and flooded lakes. The other camps withdrew, but Tuanxiao alone held the isolated city while rebels surrounded it for miles and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 摶霄坐城上，遣偏將以騎士由四門突出賊後，約曰：「旗一麾即還。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao sat on the city wall and sent a deputy general with cavalry to burst out through the four gates behind the bandits, with this agreement: "At one wave of the flag, return at once."
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao remained on the wall and sent a deputy general with cavalry to burst through all four gates and strike the enemy rear, with orders to return at a single wave of the flag.

sentences.zh: 」既而旗動，騎士還，步卒自城中出，夾擊之，賊大敗。

translations.literal: "Before long the flag moved; the cavalry returned, and foot soldiers sallied from the city to attack from both sides. The bandits were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the flag waved the cavalry wheeled back, infantry poured from the gates, and the army closed in from both sides. The rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 然賊寨猶阻西行之路，乃結陣而往，翊以奇兵，轉戰數十合，軍始得至海寧。

translations.literal: Yet bandit stockades still blocked the road westward. He therefore formed ranks and advanced, supported by surprise troops, and after several tens of engagements the army was finally able to reach Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel camps still blocked the road west, so he advanced in battle formation with flanking detachments, fighting through dozens of engagements before the army finally reached Haining.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其功，升同僉淮南行樞密院事。

translations.literal: The court praised his merit and promoted him to associate director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his achievements and promoted him to associate director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 摶霄建議於朝曰：

translations.literal: Tuanxiao submitted a proposal to the court, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao submitted the following proposal to the court:

sentences.zh: 淮安為南北襟喉、江淮要沖之地，其地一失，兩淮皆未易復也。

translations.literal: Huai'an is the throat joining north and south and a vital crossing of the Jiang and Huai. Once that place is lost, both banks of the Huai will not be easy to recover.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an is the strategic hinge between north and south and the vital crossing of the Yangzi and Huai. Once it falls, recovering the two Huai regions will be exceedingly difficult.

sentences.zh: 則救援淮安，誠為急務。

translations.literal: Therefore relief of Huai'an is truly an urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving Huai'an must therefore be treated as the most urgent priority.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，莫若於黃河上下，並瀕淮海之地，及南自沭陽，北抵沂、莒、贛榆諸州縣，布連珠營，每三十里設一總寨，就三十里中又設一小寨，使斥堠烽燧相望，而巡邏往來，遇賊則並力野戰，無事則屯種而食。

translations.literal: For planning today, there is nothing better than along the upper and lower Yellow River, together with the lands bordering the Huai and sea, and from Shuyang in the south northward to the prefectures and counties of Yi, Ju, and Ganyu—deploying linked-bead camps, establishing one main stockade every thirty li, and within each thirty li also establishing one small stockade, so that scouts and beacon towers face one another, patrols come and go, and when bandits are encountered they join forces for field battle; when there is no business they garrison, cultivate, and eat.
translations.idiomatic: For the present crisis, I propose establishing a chain of fortified camps along the Yellow River, along the Huai and sea coasts, and from Shuyang in the south to Yi, Ju, Ganyu, and neighboring counties in the north. Every thirty li should have a main stockade, with a smaller outpost midway between. Scouts and beacon towers should line the route, patrols should circulate constantly, and when rebels appear the garrisons should unite for battle; in peacetime they should farm for their own subsistence.

sentences.zh: 然後進有援，退有守，此善戰者所以常為不可勝，以待敵之可勝也。

translations.literal: Then in advance there will be support, in retreat there will be defense—this is how skilled warriors constantly make themselves unconquerable while waiting for the enemy to become conquerable.
translations.idiomatic: Thus advance will always have support and retreat will always have a defense. This is how a skilled commander keeps himself invincible while waiting for the enemy to become vulnerable.

sentences.zh: 又海寧一境，不通舟楫，軍糧惟可陸運，而凡瀕淮海之地，人民屢經盜賊，宜加存撫，權令軍人搬運。

translations.literal: Moreover, throughout the territory of Haining boats and oars cannot pass; army grain can only be transported by land. Yet in all the lands bordering the Huai and sea the people have repeatedly suffered from bandits and robbers; they should be given added care and relief, and for the time being soldiers should be ordered to carry the transport.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Haining region is inaccessible by boat, so army grain must go by land. The people along the Huai and sea coasts have suffered repeatedly from bandit raids and deserve relief and protection. For the present, soldiers should be assigned to carry the grain.

sentences.zh: 其陸運之方，每人行十步，三十六人可行一里，三百六十人可行一十里，三千六百人可行一百里。

translations.literal: The method of land transport is this: each man walks ten paces; thirty-six men can cover one li, three hundred sixty men can cover ten li, and three thousand six hundred men can cover one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The method of overland transport is as follows: each man walks ten paces. Thirty-six men span one li, three hundred sixty span ten li, and three thousand six hundred span one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 每人負米四斗，以夾布囊盛之，用印封識，人不息肩，米不著地，排列成行，日行五百回，計路二十八里，輕行一十四里，重行一十四里，日可運米二百石。

translations.literal: Each man carries four dou of rice, stored in double cloth sacks, sealed with an official stamp. Men do not rest their shoulders, and rice does not touch the ground. Arranged in rows, they make five hundred circuits per day. The route totals twenty-eight li: fourteen li going light and fourteen li going heavy. Each day two hundred shi of rice can be transported.
translations.idiomatic: Each man carries four dou of rice in paired cloth sacks, sealed with an official stamp. Shoulders never rest and grain never touches the ground. Lined up in ranks, the carriers make five hundred relays per day over a route of twenty-eight li—fourteen li outbound empty and fourteen li returning loaded—moving two hundred shi of grain daily.

sentences.zh: 每運給米一升，可供二萬人。

translations.literal: Each shi transported supplies one sheng of rice, which can sustain twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Each shi of grain transported yields one sheng per man, enough to feed twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 此百里一日運糧之術也。

translations.literal: This is the method of transporting grain one hundred li in one day.
translations.idiomatic: This is the method for moving grain one hundred li in a single day.

sentences.zh: 又江淮流移之民，並安東、海寧、沭陽、贛榆等州縣俱廢，其民壯者既為軍，老弱無所依歸者，宜設置軍民防禦司，擇軍官材堪牧守者，使居其職，而籍其民，以屯故地。

translations.literal: Moreover, the displaced people of the Jiang and Huai, together with the prefectures and counties of Andong, Haining, Shuyang, Ganyu, and others, are all abandoned. Their able-bodied men have already become soldiers, while the old and weak have nowhere to depend or return. A bureau for military-civilian defense should be established; military officers of talent fit for governing and guarding should be chosen to hold these posts, and the people should be registered to garrison their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced people of the Jiang and Huai regions, together with the abandoned prefectures and counties of Andong, Haining, Shuyang, and Ganyu, also require attention. Able-bodied men have already been drafted into the army, while the old and weak have nowhere to turn. A military-civilian defense bureau should be established, staffed with officers capable of governing, to register the people and resettle them on their former lands.

sentences.zh: 於是練兵積穀，且耕且戰，內全山東完固之邦，外禦淮海出沒之寇，而後恢復可圖也。

translations.literal: Thereby troops would be trained and grain accumulated, farming and fighting at once, securing within the intact domain of Shandong and defending without against the bandits appearing and vanishing on the Huai and sea—only then could recovery be contemplated.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the army could train and stockpile grain, fighting while farming, securing Shandong within and holding off the raiders of the Huai and sea without. Only then would recovery become possible.

sentences.zh: 十七年，毛貴陷益都、般陽等路，有旨命摶霄從知樞密院事卜蘭奚討之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Mao Gui took Yidu, Banyang, and other circuits. An imperial order commanded Tuanxiao to follow the Bureau of Military Affairs director Bulanxi in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357), Mao Gui captured Yidu, Banyang, and other circuits. An imperial edict ordered Tuanxiao to join Bureau of Military Affairs Director Bulanxi in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 而濟南又告急，摶霄乃提兵援濟南。

translations.literal: But Jinan again reported emergency, and Tuanxiao therefore led troops to relieve Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan then sent urgent appeals for help, and Tuanxiao marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 賊眾自南山來攻濟南，望之兩山皆赤。

translations.literal: Bandit forces came from the southern mountains to attack Jinan; gazing at them, both mountains were red.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces descended from the southern mountains to attack Jinan, and from a distance both hillsides seemed awash in red.

sentences.zh: 摶霄按兵城中，先以數十騎挑之，賊眾悉來鬥，騎兵少卻，至磵上，伏兵起，遂合戰，城中兵又大出，大破之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao held his army in the city. First he sent several tens of cavalry to provoke them; the bandit host all came to fight. The cavalry retreated slightly to the ravine, hidden troops rose up, and they joined battle. Troops from the city also poured out greatly, and the bandits were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao kept his army in the city and sent several dozen horsemen to provoke the enemy. The whole rebel host surged forward in response. The cavalry feigned retreat to a ravine, where hidden troops sprang up and joined the fight. Troops then poured from the city gates, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 而般陽賊复約泰安之黨，逾南山來襲濟南。

translations.literal: But the bandits of Banyang again joined with the faction of Tai'an, crossed the southern mountains, and came to raid Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: The Banyang rebels then joined forces with allies from Tai'an, crossed the southern mountains, and struck at Jinan again.

sentences.zh: 摶霄列兵城上，弗為動。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao arrayed troops on the city wall and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao lined his troops along the wall and held his position.

sentences.zh: 賊夜攻南門，獨以矢石御之。

translations.literal: At night the bandits attacked the south gate; he repelled them with arrows and stones alone.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked the south gate by night, and he repelled them with arrows and stones alone.

sentences.zh: 黎明，乃默開東門，放兵出賊後。

translations.literal: At dawn he silently opened the east gate and released troops behind the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he quietly opened the east gate and sent troops out behind the enemy.

sentences.zh: 既旦，城上兵皆下，大開南門合擊之，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Once it was fully day, the troops on the wall all came down, the south gate was opened wide, and they joined in striking the bandits. The bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When morning came the troops descended from the walls, the south gate swung wide, and the army closed in from both sides. The rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 复追殺之，賊眾悉無遺者。

translations.literal: He again pursued and killed them; the bandit host left none surviving.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and cut them down until not one rebel remained.

sentences.zh: 於是濟南始寧。

translations.literal: Jinan was thus first pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan was at last restored to peace.

sentences.zh: 詔就升淮南行樞密院副使，兼山東宣慰使都元帥，仍賜上尊、金帶、楮幣、名馬以勞之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately promoted him to vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently commander-in-chief of the Shandong Pacification Commission, and moreover bestowed fine wine, a gold belt, paper currency, and a famous horse to reward his labors.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately promoted him to vice director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and commander-in-chief of the Shandong Pacification Commission, and rewarded him with fine wine, a gold belt, paper currency, and a prized horse.

sentences.zh: 有疾其功者，譖於總兵太尉紐的該，令摶霄依前詔，從卜蘭奚同徵益都。

translations.literal: Those who resented his achievements slandered him to the commander-in-chief Grand Marshal Niudigai, causing Tuanxiao to be ordered, according to the earlier edict, to follow Bulanxi jointly on the campaign against Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Envious of his success, some officials slandered him to Grand Marshal Niudigai, commander-in-chief of the army, who ordered Tuanxiao to obey the earlier edict and join Bulanxi on the campaign against Yidu.

sentences.zh: 摶霄即出濟南城，屬老且病，請以其弟昂霄代領其眾，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao immediately departed Jinan city. As he was old and ill, he requested that his younger brother Angxiao replace him in leading his troops; the court consented.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao then left Jinan. Being old and ill, he asked that his younger brother Angxiao take command of his troops in his stead, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 授昂霄淮南行樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Angxiao was appointed judge of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao was appointed judge of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有旨命摶霄守河間之長蘆。

translations.literal: Before long, an imperial order commanded Tuanxiao to guard Changlu in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, an imperial edict ordered Tuanxiao to hold Changlu in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，摶霄以兵北行，且曰：「我去，濟南必不可保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Tuanxiao marched north with troops, saying, "When I leave, Jinan certainly cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1358), Tuanxiao marched north with his army, saying, "Once I am gone, Jinan will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 」既而濟南果陷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jinan indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan did indeed fall soon after.

sentences.zh: 摶霄方駐兵南皮縣之魏家莊，適有使者奉詔拜摶霄河南行省右丞，甫拜命，毛貴兵已至，而營壘猶未完。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao was then encamped at Weijiazhuang in Nanpi County when an envoy arrived with an edict appointing him Right Vice Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat. He had just received the appointment when Mao Gui's troops already arrived, and the camp fortifications were still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao was encamped at Weijiazhuang in Nanpi County when an envoy arrived bearing an edict appointing him Right Vice Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat. He had barely accepted the commission when Mao Gui's forces appeared, and the camp defenses were not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂摶霄曰：「賊至當如何？

translations.literal: The generals said to Tuanxiao, "When the bandits arrive, what should we do?
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked Tuanxiao, "What are we to do when the rebels arrive?

sentences.zh: 」摶霄曰：「我受命至此，當以死報國耳。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said, "Having received my commission to come here, I ought to repay the state with my death, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao replied, "I was sent here on imperial commission. I can only repay the dynasty with my life.

sentences.zh: 」因拔劍督兵以戰。

translations.literal: He therefore drew his sword and urged the troops into battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew his sword and led his men into battle.

sentences.zh: 而賊眾突至摶霄前，捽而問曰：「汝為誰？

translations.literal: Bandit forces suddenly rushed before Tuanxiao, seized him, and asked, "Who are you?
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops suddenly surged up to Tuanxiao, seized him, and demanded, "Who are you?

sentences.zh: 」摶霄曰：「我董老爺也！

translations.literal: Tuanxiao said, "I am Lord Dong!
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao answered, "I am Lord Dong!

sentences.zh: 」眾刺殺之，無血，惟見其有白氣沖天。

translations.literal: The crowd stabbed and killed him. There was no blood; only white vapor was seen rushing skyward.
translations.idiomatic: The mob stabbed him to death. No blood flowed; only a white vapor was seen rising into the sky.

sentences.zh: 是日，昂霄亦死之。

translations.literal: That same day Angxiao also died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Angxiao was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈宣忠守正保節功臣、榮祿大夫、河南行省平章政事、柱國，追封魏國公，諡忠定。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Proclaims Loyalty, Upholds Integrity, and Preserves Righteousness, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei; given the posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Subject Who Proclaims Loyalty, Upholds Integrity, and Preserves Righteousness, given the rank of Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Wei, and granted the posthumous name Zhongding.

sentences.zh: 昂霄贈推誠孝節功臣、嘉議大夫、禮部尚書、上輕車都尉，追封隴西郡侯，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: Angxiao was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Filial Righteousness, Grand Master for Deliberation, Minister of Rites, and Superior Commandant of Light Chariots; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi Commandery; given the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Angxiao was posthumously honored as Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Filial Righteousness, given the rank of Grand Master for Deliberation, Minister of Rites, and Superior Commandant of Light Chariots, enfeoffed posthumously as Marquis of Longxi Commandery, and granted the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 摶霄早以儒生起家，輒為能吏，會天下大亂，乃復以武功自奮，其才略有大過人者，而當時用之不能盡其才，君子惜之。

translations.literal: Tuanxiao had early risen from the ranks of Confucian scholars and was always a capable official. When the realm fell into great disorder, he again exerted himself through military achievement. His talent and strategy greatly surpassed others, yet those who employed him at the time could not fully use his abilities. Men of principle regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Tuanxiao had begun his career as a Confucian scholar and quickly proved himself a capable administrator. When the empire descended into chaos, he distinguished himself anew through military service. His talent and strategic ability far exceeded those of ordinary men, yet the court of his day never fully employed his gifts. Reflective observers have lamented the waste.

sentences.zh: ○劉哈剌不花

translations.literal: Liu Halabuhua
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabuhua

sentences.zh: 劉哈剌不花，其先江西人。

translations.literal: Liu Halabuhua's ancestors were men of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabuhua's family originally came from Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 倜儻好義，不事家產，有古俠士風。

translations.literal: Unconstrained and fond of righteousness, he did not attend to family property and had the air of an ancient knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited and devoted to righteousness, he cared little for family wealth and carried himself in the manner of the knights-errant of old.

sentences.zh: 居燕趙有年，遂為探馬赤軍戶。

translations.literal: After residing in Yan and Zhao for many years, he became a household of the tamachi army.
translations.idiomatic: After living in the Yan and Zhao region for many years, he became registered as a tamachi soldier.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，潁、亳盜起，朝遷以泰不花為河南行省平章政事，總兵討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, bandits rose in Ying and Bo. The court transferred Taibuhua to be Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat and placed him in overall command of troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng (1352), rebels broke out in Ying and Bo. The court appointed Taibuhua Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat and put him in command of the campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花上書陳十事，其七言兵機及攻守方略。

translations.literal: Halabuhua submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters, seven of which concerned military opportunities and strategies of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua submitted a memorial outlining ten proposals, seven of them devoted to military timing and offensive and defensive strategy.

sentences.zh: 泰不花大喜，即辟為掾史。

translations.literal: Taibuhua was greatly pleased and immediately recruited him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua was greatly impressed and immediately took him on as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，奏除左右司都事。

translations.literal: Before long, a memorial was submitted appointing him director of the Left and Right Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted by memorial to director of the Left and Right Secretariats.

sentences.zh: 泰不花以哈剌不花嘗為探馬赤，有膂力，善騎射，俾統前八翼軍，為先鋒將。

translations.literal: Because Halabuhua had once been a tamachi soldier, possessed great physical strength, and was skilled in horsemanship and archery, Taibuhua had him command the front eight wings of the army as vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: Because Halabuhua had served as a tamachi soldier, possessed exceptional strength, and excelled at horsemanship and archery, Taibuhua put him in command of the front eight wings of the army as vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 明號令，信賞罰，士皆樂為之用，而料敵成敗，所向無失。

translations.literal: He made orders clear, kept rewards and punishments trustworthy, and the troops all gladly served under him. In judging the enemy's success or failure, wherever he went he never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced clear orders and kept his rewards and punishments reliable, so his men served him willingly. In reading the enemy's strengths and weaknesses, he never failed to prevail.

sentences.zh: 是時，答失八都魯軍潰於長葛，收集散卒，复屯中牟。

translations.literal: At this time Chaghan Temur's army was routed at Changge; he gathered scattered soldiers and again encamped at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Chaghan Temur's army was routed at Changge. He gathered his scattered troops and reestablished camp at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花軍於汴梁南彭子岡。

translations.literal: Halabuhua encamped his army at Pengzigang south of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua encamped his army at Pengzigang, south of Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 有自長葛來者言，總兵官已為賊所敗，次中牟。

translations.literal: Someone coming from Changge reported that the commander-in-chief had already been defeated by bandits and was now at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: A messenger from Changge reported that the commander-in-chief had already been defeated by the rebels and was now at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花曰：「賊既捷，兵必再至，我不可不往援。

translations.literal: Halabuhua said, "Since the bandits have won, their troops will surely come again. We cannot fail to go to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua said, "The rebels have won once; their troops will surely strike again. We must go to his aid.

sentences.zh: 」遂整兵而前。

translations.literal: He therefore arrayed his troops and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He then marshaled his troops and marched forward.

sentences.zh: 既而有使馳報：夜四鼓，賊從洧川渡河，未知其所向。

translations.literal: Then a messenger came at full speed with a report: at the fourth watch of the night, bandits crossed the river from Weichuan, and it was not yet known where they were headed.
translations.idiomatic: Then a courier arrived with urgent news: at the fourth watch of the night, rebels had crossed the river from Weichuan, and their destination was still unknown.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花曰：「是必襲答失八都魯營耳。

translations.literal: Halabuhua said, "They must be raiding Chaghan Temur's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua said, "They must be striking at Chaghan Temur's camp.

sentences.zh: 我行已緩，不及事，不若以精銳斷賊歸路，覆之必矣。

translations.literal: Our march is already slow and will not arrive in time for the affair. It would be better to use elite troops to cut off the bandits' line of retreat; overturning them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: We are already too late to intervene in time. Better to deploy elite troops to cut off the rebels' retreat; we can surely destroy them that way.

sentences.zh: 」於是領軍徐行。

translations.literal: He therefore led the army forward at a leisurely pace.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore led his army forward at a deliberate pace.

sentences.zh: 天未明，伏軍其歸路。

translations.literal: Before dawn, he hid troops along their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn he placed ambush troops along their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 賊果襲答失八都魯營，大掠輜重而回。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed raided Chaghan Temur's camp, plundered the baggage train heavily, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did indeed raid Chaghan Temur's camp, plundered his baggage train, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花伏軍四起，賊大敗，盡俘獲之。

translations.literal: Halabuhua's hidden troops rose on all sides; the bandits were greatly defeated and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua's ambush forces rose on every side. The rebels were routed and all were captured.

sentences.zh: 當是時，答失八都魯雖以平章政事總大兵，而哈剌不花功名與之相埒。

translations.literal: At that time, although Chaghan Temur held overall command of the great army as chief administrator, Halabuhua's achievements and fame were equal to his.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, although Chaghan Temur held overall command of the army as chief administrator, Halabuhua's achievements and reputation matched his own.

sentences.zh: 十七年，山東毛貴率其賊眾，由河間趨直沽，遂犯漷州，至棗林。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Mao Gui of Shandong led his bandit host from Hejian toward Zhigu, then attacked Huo Prefecture and reached Zaolin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357), Mao Gui of Shandong led his rebel forces from Hejian toward Zhigu, then attacked Huo Prefecture and reached Zaolin.

sentences.zh: 已而略柳林，逼畿甸，樞密副使達國珍戰死，京師人心大駭。

translations.literal: Before long he plundered Liulin, pressed upon the capital region, and Daguozhen, associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, died in battle. The hearts of the people in the capital were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He then plundered Liulin and pressed toward the capital region. Daguozhen, associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was killed in battle, and panic seized the capital.

sentences.zh: 在廷之臣，或勸乘輿北巡以避之，或勸遷都關陝，眾議紛然，獨左丞相太平執不可。

translations.literal: Among the ministers at court, some urged the emperor to tour north in the imperial carriage to avoid them, some urged moving the capital to the Guan and Shan region, and opinions were confused and numerous. Only Left Chancellor Taiping held that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At court some officials urged the emperor to tour north to escape the rebels, others urged relocating the capital to the Guanzhong region, and debate raged on all sides, but Left Chancellor Taiping alone insisted that neither course must be taken.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花時為同知樞密院事，奉詔以兵拒之，與之戰於柳林，大捷。

translations.literal: Halabuhua was then associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. By imperial order he led troops to resist them and fought them at Liulin, winning a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua was then associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. By imperial order he led troops to meet the enemy and fought them at Liulin, winning a great victory.

sentences.zh: 貴眾悉潰退，走據濟南，京師遂安，哈剌不花之功居多。

translations.literal: Gui's host all broke and retreated, fled, and held Jinan. The capital was thus secured, and Halabuhua's achievement in this was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Gui's forces broke and fled, retreating to hold Jinan. The capital was thus secured, and Halabuhua's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花後遷河南行省平章政事以卒。

translations.literal: Halabuhua was later transferred to Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Halabuhua was later promoted to Chief Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, in which post he died.

sentences.zh: 初，哈剌不花與信州人倪晦字孟晰同事泰不花為掾史。

translations.literal: At first Halabuhua and Ni Hui of Xin Prefecture, courtesy name Mengxi, served together under Taibuhua as clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Halabuhua and Ni Hui of Xin Prefecture, courtesy name Mengxi, had served together as clerks under Taibuhua.

sentences.zh: 晦涉書史，精文墨，機識警敏，泰不花深委任之，言無不從；

translations.literal: Hui was versed in books and history, skilled in writing, quick and alert in wit and judgment. Taibuhua deeply entrusted affairs to him, and in whatever he spoke there was none not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Hui was well read in history and skilled in writing, quick-witted and perceptive. Taibuhua relied on him deeply and never refused his counsel.

sentences.zh: 而哈剌不花或有所論白，多沮不行，由是心銜泰不花。

translations.literal: But when Halabuhua sometimes offered proposals, most were blocked and not carried out. Because of this he harbored resentment in his heart toward Taibuhua.
translations.idiomatic: When Halabuhua offered proposals of his own, however, most were blocked and never adopted, and he came to bear a grudge against Taibuhua.

sentences.zh: 及泰不花事敗，走詣哈剌不花求援，而哈剌不花不能曲為保全，乃縛泰不花送京師，致之死地，君子以是少之。

translations.literal: When Taibuhua's affairs failed, he fled and went to Halabuhua seeking aid. But Halabuhua could not bend matters to preserve him; he therefore bound Taibuhua and sent him to the capital, bringing about his death. Men of principle therefore thought less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Taibuhua's cause collapsed, he fled to Halabuhua seeking help. Halabuhua could not bring himself to protect him, however, and instead bound Taibuhua and sent him to the capital, ensuring his death. Reflective observers have held this against him.

sentences.zh: ○王英

translations.literal: Wang Ying
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying

sentences.zh: 王英，字邦傑，益都人。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, courtesy name Bangjie, was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, courtesy name Bangjie, was a native of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性剛果，有大節，膂力絕人，善騎射。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute, possessed of great integrity, with physical strength surpassing others, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was resolute and decisive, possessed of great integrity, with exceptional strength and skill in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，為莒州翼千戶。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post and became centurion of the Juzhou wing.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post and became centurion of the Juzhou wing.

sentences.zh: 父子皆善用雙刀，人號之曰刀王。

translations.literal: Father and son were both skilled in using paired sabers, and people called them the Saber Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were both masters of the paired saber, and people called them the Saber Kings.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，江西行樞密院命帥師南雄，討賊丘大老。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, the Jiangxi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs ordered him to command troops at Nanxiong to suppress the bandit Qiu Dalao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan (1292), the Jiangxi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs ordered him to lead troops at Nanxiong against the rebel Qiu Dalao.

sentences.zh: 賊六百餘人突至，英與戰，殺其渠帥劉把東，獲九十餘人。

translations.literal: More than six hundred bandits suddenly arrived. Ying fought them, killed their chieftain Liu Badong, and captured more than ninety men.
translations.idiomatic: More than six hundred rebels suddenly appeared. Ying engaged them, killed their leader Liu Badong, and captured more than ninety men.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，從左丞董士選討大山賊劉貴，擒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzheng, he followed Left Vice Chancellor Dong Shixuan in suppressing the bandit Liu Gui of Dashan and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzheng (1295), he followed Left Vice Chancellor Dong Shixuan in suppressing the Dashan rebel Liu Gui and captured him.

sentences.zh: 二年，討永新、安福二州賊，餘黨皆息。

translations.literal: In the second year, he suppressed bandits in the two prefectures of Yongxin and Anfu, and the remaining factions all subsided.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he suppressed rebels in Yongxin and Anfu prefectures, and the remaining bands were pacified.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，寧都賊起，行省命英率各萬戶軍討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, bandits rose in Ningdu. The branch secretariat ordered Ying to lead the armies of the various ten-thousand-household officers to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanyou (1315), rebels broke out in Ningdu. The branch secretariat ordered Ying to lead the armies of the various ten-thousand-household officers against them.

sentences.zh: 賊勢甚張，英屢戰皆勝，斬獲不可勝數，積尸盈野，水為不流。

translations.literal: The bandit force was very strong. Ying fought repeatedly and always won. Those killed and captured were beyond counting; corpses piled up and filled the fields, and the water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel force was formidable, but Ying fought repeatedly and always prevailed. The slain and captured were beyond counting; corpses piled across the fields until the water ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 行省平章李世安，遣英迓江浙平章張閭所領軍於閩境，至木麻坑，擒賊蔡五九。

translations.literal: Li Shi'an, chief administrator of the branch secretariat, dispatched Ying to meet the army led by Zhang Lu, chief administrator of the Jiang and Zhe Branch Secretariat, at the Fujian border. At Mumakeng he captured the bandit Cai Wujiu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi'an, chief administrator of the branch secretariat, sent Ying to meet the army led by Zhang Lu, chief administrator of the Jiang and Zhe Branch Secretariat, at the Fujian border. At Mumakeng he captured the rebel Cai Wujiu.

sentences.zh: 又追賊至上虎嶂，遇賊三千餘人，盡殲之。

translations.literal: He again pursued bandits to Shanghuzhang, encountered more than three thousand bandits, and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then pursued rebels to Shanghuzhang, encountered more than three thousand of them, and annihilated them all.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，以大臣薦，授忠武校尉、益都淄萊萬戶府副千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, on recommendation of a high minister, he was appointed Colonel Who Maintains Martial Integrity and deputy centurion of the Yidu Zilai Ten-Thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi (1321), on the recommendation of a senior official, he was appointed Colonel Who Maintains Martial Integrity and deputy centurion of the Yidu Zilai Ten-Thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，授宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli, he was appointed General Who Proclaims Military Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianli (1328), he was appointed General Who Proclaims Military Might.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，行省命英招捕桂陽州賊張思進等二千人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun, the branch secretariat ordered Ying to summon and capture the two thousand bandits of Guiyang Prefecture, Zhang Sijin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun (1331), the branch secretariat ordered Ying to summon and capture the two thousand rebels of Guiyang Prefecture led by Zhang Sijin and others.

sentences.zh: 英至，布以威信，皆相率請降。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived, he spread authority and trust, and they all led one another in requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying arrived, he won them over with authority and good faith, and they all came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，授懷遠大將軍、同知海北海南道宣慰使司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, he was appointed Grand General of Expansive Far-reaching and associate commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong (1333), he was appointed Grand General of Expansive Far-reaching and associate commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，萬安軍賊吳汝期等作亂，聚眾三千人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, the bandits of Wan'an Army, Wu Ruqi and others, rebelled and gathered a host of three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan, the Wan'an Army rebels Wu Ruqi and others rose in revolt and gathered a force of three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 英至，賊皆就擒。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived, the bandits were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying arrived, the rebels were all captured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李志甫起漳州，劉虎仔起潮州，詔命江西行省右丞燕帖木兒討之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zhipu rose in Zhang Prefecture and Liu Huzai rose in Chao Prefecture. An edict ordered El Temur, Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Zhipu rebelled in Zhang Prefecture and Liu Huzai in Chao Prefecture. An edict ordered El Temur, Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 方賊起時，英已致仕，平章政事伯撒里謂僚佐曰：「是雖鼠竊狗偷，非刀王行不可。

translations.literal: Just as the bandits rose, Ying had already retired from office. Chief Administrator Barsuri said to his staff, "Although these are petty thefts like rats and dogs, without the Saber King going it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels broke out, Ying had already retired. Chief Administrator Barsuri told his staff, "Petty as these raids may be, nothing will succeed unless the Saber King goes.

sentences.zh: 其人雖投老，必可以義激。

translations.literal: Although the man has reached old age, he can surely be roused by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Though he is old, he can surely be moved by a call to duty.

sentences.zh: 」乃使迎致之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent someone to welcome and bring him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent envoys to invite him back.

sentences.zh: 英曰：「國家有事，吾雖老，其可坐視乎！

translations.literal: Ying said, "When the state has an affair, although I am old, how can I sit and watch!
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "When the state is in need, how can I, though old, sit idle!

sentences.zh: 」據鞍橫槊，精神飛動，馳赴焉。

translations.literal: He mounted the saddle, held his spear crosswise, his spirit soaring and active, and galloped off to join them.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted his horse, spear in hand, his spirit afire, and galloped to the front.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，英功居多。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Ying's achievement was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Ying's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 至正中，毛貴陷益都，英時年九十有六，乃謂其子弘曰：「我世受國恩，美官厚祿，備嘗享之。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng period, Mao Gui took Yidu. Ying was then ninety-six years old. He said to his son Hong, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations. Fine offices and generous salaries—we have fully tasted and enjoyed them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng period, Mao Gui captured Yidu. Ying was then ninety-six years old. He said to his son Hong, "Our family has enjoyed the state's favor for generations. We have held fine offices and generous salaries and tasted every comfort they bring.

sentences.zh: 今老矣，縱不能事戎馬以報天子，尚忍食異姓之粟以求生乎！

translations.literal: Now I am old. Even if I cannot serve in arms and horses to repay the Son of Heaven, how can I still bear to eat grain of another surname in order to preserve life!
translations.idiomatic: I am old now. Even if I can no longer serve on horseback to repay the emperor, how can I still eat a rebel's grain merely to stay alive!

sentences.zh: 」水漿不入口者數日，遂卒。

translations.literal: For several days he took neither water nor broth, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: For several days he took neither food nor water, and then he died.

sentences.zh: 毛貴聞之，使具棺衾以葬。

translations.literal: When Mao Gui heard of it, he had a coffin and burial shroud prepared for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Gui heard of it, he had a coffin and burial shroud prepared for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 將斂，舉其屍不動，焚香祝曰：「公子弘請公歸葬先塋。

translations.literal: When they were about to enclose the body, they lifted the corpse but it did not move. They burned incense and prayed, saying, "Your son Hong asks that you, sir, return to be buried in the ancestral grave.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to lay him in the coffin, they lifted the body but it would not move. They burned incense and prayed, "Your son Hong asks that you return to be buried in the ancestral grave.

sentences.zh: 」祝畢，屍遂起，觀者莫不驚異。

translations.literal: When the prayer was finished, the corpse then rose. Those who watched were all startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was finished, the body rose. All who witnessed it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 山東宣慰使普顏不花及憲司請卹典於朝，有曰：「不食寇粟，餓死芹泉，有夷、齊之風，為臣之清者也。

translations.literal: Puyan Buhua, pacification commissioner of Shandong, and the censorate requested mourning honors from the court. Someone said, "Refusing to eat the bandits' grain and starving to death at Qinquan—he had the air of Bo Yi and Shu Qi; this is the purity of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Puyan Buhua, pacification commissioner of Shandong, and the censorate petitioned the court for mourning honors. One memorialist wrote, "Refusing the rebels' grain and starving to death at Qinquan, he showed the spirit of Bo Yi and Shu Qi—the integrity of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」芹泉，谷名，英所居也。

translations.literal: Qinquan is the name of a valley where Ying lived.
translations.idiomatic: Qinquan was the name of the valley where Ying had lived.

sentences.zh: ○石抹宜孫

translations.literal: Shimoyisun
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyisun

sentences.zh: 石抹宜孫，字申之。

translations.literal: Shimoyisun, courtesy name Shenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shimoyisun, courtesy name Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 其先遼之迪烈糺人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Diliejiu people of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were Diliejiu people of the Liao dynasty.

sentences.zh: 五世祖曰也先，事太祖為御史大夫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was called Yexian, who served the Taizu as Censor-in-Chief and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yexian served Taizu as Censor-in-Chief and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 也先之曾孫曰繼祖，字伯善，襲父職，為沿海上副萬戶。

translations.literal: Yexian's great-grandson was called Jizu, courtesy name Boshan, who inherited his father's post and became deputy ten-thousand-household officer of the Coastal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yexian's great-grandson Jizu, courtesy name Boshan, inherited his father's post and became deputy commander of the Coastal Guard.

sentences.zh: 初以沿海軍分鎮台州，皇慶元年，又移鎮婺、處兩州。

translations.literal: At first he garrisoned Taizhou with the coastal army in divided posts. In the first year of Huangqing, he was again transferred to garrison the two prefectures of Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At first he garrisoned Taizhou with detachments of the coastal army. In the first year of Huangqing (1312), he was transferred to garrison Wu and Chu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴肅，平寧都寇，有戰功；

translations.literal: In commanding troops he was stern and strict. He pacified the bandits of Ningdu and had military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his troops with stern discipline, pacified the Ningdu rebels, and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 且明達政事，講究鹽策，多合時宜。

translations.literal: Moreover he was clear and penetrating in government affairs, studied salt policy, and much accorded with the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was also clear-sighted in administration, studied salt policy closely, and devised measures well suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 為學本於經術，而兼通名法、縱橫、天文、地理、術數、方技、釋老之說，見稱薦紳間。

translations.literal: In learning he took the classics as his foundation, yet was also versed in legalism, coalition diplomacy, astronomy, geography, numerology, medicine and craft, and Buddhist and Daoist teachings, and was praised among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship was rooted in the classics, yet he was also versed in law, statecraft, astronomy, geography, divination, medicine, and Buddhist and Daoist learning, and was praised among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 宜孫其子也。

translations.literal: Yisun was his son.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was his son.

sentences.zh: 宜孫性警敏，嗜學問，於書務博覽，而長於詩歌。

translations.literal: Yisun was by nature alert and quick, fond of learning, in books striving for broad reading, and skilled in poetry and song.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was quick-witted by nature, devoted to learning, widely read, and accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 嘗借嫡弟厚孫廕，襲父職，為沿海上副萬戶，守處州。

translations.literal: He once borrowed his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege, inherited his father's post, became deputy ten-thousand-household officer of the Coastal Guard, and guarded Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once used his younger brother Housun's hereditary privilege to inherit his father's post as deputy commander of the Coastal Guard and took charge of defending Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及弟長，即讓其職還之，退居台州。

translations.literal: When his brother came of age, he immediately yielded the post and returned it to him, retiring to reside in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother came of age, he immediately returned the post to him and retired to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，方國珍起海上，江浙行省檄宜孫守溫州，宜孫即起任其事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng, Fang Guozhen rose on the sea. The Jiang and Zhe Branch Secretariat issued an order to Yisun to guard Wenzhou, and Yisun immediately rose to take up the task.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng (1351), Fang Guozhen rose on the sea. The Jiang and Zhe Branch Secretariat ordered Yisun to defend Wenzhou, and he immediately took up the assignment.

sentences.zh: 其年閩寇犯處州，复檄宜孫以兵平之。

translations.literal: That same year Fujian bandits invaded Chuzhou, and again an order was issued to Yisun to pacify them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Fujian rebels invaded Chuzhou, and he was again ordered to pacify them by force.

sentences.zh: 以功升浙東宣慰副使，分府於台州。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Eastern Zhe Pacification Commission, with his office divided at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Eastern Zhe Pacification Commission, with his headquarters at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，處之屬縣山寇並起，宜孫復奉省檄往討之。

translations.literal: Before long, mountain bandits rose together in the subordinate counties of Chu Prefecture, and Yisun again received a branch secretariat order to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long mountain rebels rose simultaneously in the counties subordinate to Chu Prefecture, and Yisun again received orders from the branch secretariat to go suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至則築處州城，為御敵計。

translations.literal: When he arrived he fortified Chuzhou city as a plan for resisting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he fortified the walls of Chuzhou to prepare for enemy attack.

sentences.zh: 十七年，江浙行省左丞相達識鐵睦邇承製升宜孫行樞密院判官，總制處州，分院治於處。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat Left Chancellor Dash Timur, by provisional order, promoted Yisun to vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, placed him in overall command of Chuzhou, and established a sub-office at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357), Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat Left Chancellor Dash Timur, acting on provisional authority, promoted Yisun to vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, placed him in overall command of Chuzhou, and established a sub-office there.

sentences.zh: 又以江浙儒學副提舉劉基為其院經歷，蕭山縣尹蘇友龍為照磨，而宜孫又辟郡人胡深、葉琛、章溢參謀其軍事。

translations.literal: He also appointed Jiang-Zhe Associate Commissioner for Confucian Studies Liu Ji as director of affairs for his bureau, Xiaoshan County Magistrate Su Youlong as registrar, and Yisun further recruited fellow countrymen Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi to counsel on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Ji, associate commissioner for Confucian studies in Jiang-Zhe, as director of affairs for the bureau; Su Youlong, magistrate of Xiaoshan County, as registrar; and Yisun further recruited his countrymen Hu Shen, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi as military advisers.

sentences.zh: 處為郡，山谷聯絡，盜賊憑據險阻，輒竊發，不易平治。

translations.literal: Chuzhou was a prefecture where valleys and mountains linked together; bandits relied on perilous terrain, repeatedly raided in secret, and were not easy to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou was a mountainous prefecture where valleys and ridges interlocked. Bandits exploited the rugged terrain to launch raids and were difficult to suppress.

sentences.zh: 宜孫用基等謀，或搗以兵，或誘以計，未幾，皆殲殄無遺類。

translations.literal: Yisun used the plans of Ji and the others—sometimes striking with troops, sometimes luring with stratagem—and before long all were exterminated without survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Following the counsel of Liu Ji and the others, Yisun alternately attacked with troops and enticed with stratagems. Before long the bandits were wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 尋升同僉行樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to associate director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，天下已多故，所在守將各自為計相保守。

translations.literal: At that time the realm already had many troubles; defending generals everywhere each made his own plans to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then the empire was in turmoil, and local commanders everywhere looked to their own survival.

sentences.zh: 於是浙東則宜孫在處州，邁里古思在紹興為稱首。

translations.literal: Thus in eastern Zhejiang, Yisun at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing were foremost in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern Zhejiang, Yisun at Chuzhou and Mailigusi at Shaoxing stood foremost among the defenders.

sentences.zh: 十八年十二月，大明兵取蘭溪，且逼婺，而宜孫母實在婺城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighteenth year, the Great Ming army took Lanxi and was pressing upon Wu, while Yisun's mother was actually in Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eighteenth year (1358), the Ming army captured Lanxi and advanced on Wu Prefecture, where Yisun's mother was living.

sentences.zh: 宜孫泣曰：「義莫重於君親，食祿而不事其事，是無君也；

translations.literal: Yisun wept and said: "Among obligations none is weightier than to sovereign and parent. To receive salary yet not serve one's duty—this is to be without a sovereign;"
translations.idiomatic: Yisun wept and said: "No obligation outweighs loyalty to sovereign and filial duty to parent. To draw a salary yet fail in one's duty is to betray one's sovereign;"

sentences.zh: 母在難而不赴，是無親也。

translations.literal: when one's mother is in peril yet one does not go to her—this is to be without a parent.
translations.idiomatic: to leave one's mother in danger and not go to her is to abandon one's parent.

sentences.zh: 無君無親，尚可立天地間哉！

translations.literal: Without sovereign and without parent, how can one still stand between heaven and earth!
translations.idiomatic: Without loyalty or filial piety, how can one still face the world!

sentences.zh: 」即遣胡深等將民兵數万往赴援，而親率精銳為之殿。

translations.literal: "He immediately dispatched Hu Shen and others to lead tens of thousands of militia to go and relieve her, while he personally led picked troops to serve as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Hu Shen and others with tens of thousands of militia to the rescue, while he personally led an elite force to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 兵至婺，與大明兵甫接，即敗績而還。

translations.literal: When the troops reached Wu, they had barely engaged the Great Ming army before suffering defeat and returning.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Wu Prefecture, it barely engaged the Ming forces before suffering defeat and withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 時經略使李國鳳至浙東，承製拜宜孫江浙行省參知政事，階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: At the time Pacification Commissioner Li Guofeng arrived in eastern Zhejiang and, by provisional order, appointed Yisun vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat with the rank of Grand Master for Attendant Service.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Li Guofeng had just arrived in eastern Zhejiang and, acting on provisional authority, appointed Yisun vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat with the rank of Grand Master for Attendant Service.

sentences.zh: 明年，大明兵入處州，宜孫將數十騎走福建境上，欲圖報復，而所至人心已散，事不可復為。

translations.literal: The next year the Great Ming army entered Chuzhou. Yisun led several tens of horsemen and fled to the Fujian border, intending to plan revenge, but wherever he went popular support had already dispersed and the affair could no longer be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Ming army entered Chuzhou. Yisun fled to the Fujian border with a few dozen horsemen, hoping to regroup for revenge, but morale had collapsed everywhere and the cause was lost.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「處州，吾所守者也。

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "Chuzhou is what I have defended.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "Chuzhou is the land I have defended.

sentences.zh: 今吾勢已窮，無所於往，不如還處州境，死亦為處州鬼耳！

translations.literal: Now my strength is already exhausted and I have nowhere to go. Better to return to Chuzhou territory—even in death I shall be a ghost of Chuzhou!"
