translations.idiomatic: My strength is spent and I have nowhere left to go. Better to return to Chuzhou—even in death I shall be a ghost of that land!"

sentences.zh: 」既還，至處之慶元縣，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: "When he had returned and reached Qingyuan County in Chuzhou, he was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back, but upon reaching Qingyuan County in Chuzhou he was killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷贈推誠宣力效節功臣、集賢大學士、榮祿大夫、上柱國，追封越國公，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court posthumously granted him the title Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Proclaiming Strength, and Devoted Integrity; Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies; Grand Master for Glorious Emolument; and Superior Pillar of the State. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Yisun was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister for Sincerity, Proclaiming Strength, and Devoted Integrity; Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies; Grand Master for Glorious Emolument; and Superior Pillar of the State. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 邁里古思

translations.literal: Mailigusi
translations.idiomatic: Mailigusi

sentences.zh: 邁里古思者，寧夏人也，字善卿。

translations.literal: Mailigusi was a man of Ningxia, courtesy name Shanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Mailigusi was a native of Ningxia, courtesy name Shanqing.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年進士，授紹興路錄事司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed darughachi of the Shaoxing Circuit Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourteenth year of Zhizheng (1354), he was appointed darughachi of the Shaoxing Circuit Records Office.

sentences.zh: 苗軍主將楊完者在杭，縱其軍鈔掠，莫敢誰何，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Miao Army commander-in-chief Yang Waner was at Hangzhou, letting his troops plunder and seize by force; no one dared to challenge them, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Army commander Yang Waner was stationed at Hangzhou, where his troops looted at will. No one dared resist, and the people suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 俄有至紹興城中強奪人馬者，邁里古思擒斬數人，苗軍乃懼，不敢復至其境。

translations.literal: Before long some arrived in Shaoxing city forcibly seizing people and horses. Mailigusi captured and beheaded several men, and the Miao Army then grew fearful and no longer dared enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao soldiers entered Shaoxing and began seizing people and horses by force, Mailigusi captured and executed several of them. The Miao Army grew fearful and never again entered his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 邁里古思名聲遂大振。

translations.literal: Mailigusi's reputation then greatly resounded.
translations.idiomatic: Mailigusi's reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 會江南行台移治紹興，檄邁里古思為行台鎮撫，乃大募民兵，為守禦計。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan Branch Censorate moved its seat to Shaoxing, it summoned Mailigusi as Branch Censorate pacifier. He then greatly recruited militia as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan Branch Censorate relocated to Shaoxing, it appointed Mailigusi as its pacification commissioner. He raised a large militia force to prepare the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 處州山賊焚掠婺之永康、東陽，邁里古思提兵往擊之，與石抹宜孫約期夾攻其巢穴，山賊以平。

translations.literal: Chuzhou mountain bandits burned and plundered Yongkang and Dongyang in Wu. Mailigusi led troops to strike them, and with Shimoyisun set a date for a pincer attack on their nest; the mountain bandits were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits from Chuzhou raided Yongkang and Dongyang in Wu Prefecture. Mailigusi marched against them and, coordinating with Shimoyisun for a pincer attack on their stronghold, pacified the mountain rebels.

sentences.zh: 擢江東廉訪司經歷，仍留紹興，以兵衛台治。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of affairs in the Jiangdong Commission for Investigating Censors, yet remained at Shaoxing to guard the censorate seat with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of affairs in the Jiangdong Commission for Investigating Censors while remaining at Shaoxing to garrison the censorate with troops.

sentences.zh: 時浙東、西郡縣多殘破，獨邁里古思保障紹興，境內晏然，民愛之如父母。

translations.literal: At the time eastern and western Zhejiang prefectures and counties were mostly ravaged and broken; only Mailigusi secured Shaoxing, and within his borders all was tranquil. The people loved him as they would their parents.
translations.idiomatic: While prefectures and counties across Zhejiang lay in ruins, Mailigusi alone kept Shaoxing secure and at peace. The people loved him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 江浙省臣乃承製授行樞密院判官，分院治紹興。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe provincial officials thereupon, by provisional order, appointed him vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and established a sub-office at Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe provincial officials then, acting on provisional authority, appointed him vice director of the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs with a sub-office at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 會方國珍遣兵侵紹興屬縣，邁里古思曰：「國珍本海賊，今既降，為大官，而復來害吾民，可乎！

translations.literal: When Fang Guozhen dispatched troops to invade counties under Shaoxing, Mailigusi said: "Guozhen was originally a sea bandit. Now that he has surrendered and become a great official, yet he comes again to harm our people—is this acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guozhen sent troops to raid counties under Shaoxing's jurisdiction, Mailigusi said: "Fang Guozhen was once a pirate. Now that he has surrendered and holds high office, how can he come again to harm our people!"

sentences.zh: 」欲率兵往問罪。

translations.literal: "He wished to lead troops to go and demand accountability.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved to march against Fang Guozhen and demand an accounting.

sentences.zh: 先遣部將黃中取上虞，中還，請益兵。

translations.literal: First he dispatched his subordinate general Huang Zhong to take Shangyu. Zhong returned and requested additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent his deputy Huang Zhong to capture Shangyu. Zhong returned and requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方倚重國珍，資其舟以運糧，而御史大夫拜住哥，與國珍素通賄賂，情好甚厚，憤邁里古思擅舉兵，恐且生事，即使人召邁里古思至其私第，與計事，至則命左右以鐵槌撾死之，斷其頭，擲廁溷中。

translations.literal: At this time the court was relying heavily on Guozhen, using his boats to transport grain. Censor-in-Chief Baizhuge had long exchanged bribes with Guozhen and their friendship was very close. Angered that Mailigusi had raised troops on his own authority and fearing he might cause trouble, he sent men to summon Mailigusi to his private residence to discuss affairs. When he arrived, Baizhuge ordered his attendants to beat him to death with iron mallets, sever his head, and throw it into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then relying heavily on Fang Guozhen, using his fleet to transport grain. Censor-in-Chief Baizhuge, who had long exchanged bribes with Fang and enjoyed close ties with him, was enraged that Mailigusi had mobilized troops without authorization and feared he would cause further trouble. He summoned Mailigusi to his private residence on the pretext of consultation, then ordered his attendants to beat him to death with iron mallets, sever his head, and throw it into a latrine.

sentences.zh: 城中民聞之，不問男女老幼，無不慟哭者。

translations.literal: When the people in the city heard of it, regardless of man or woman, old or young, there was none who did not wail in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of the city learned of it, men and women, old and young alike, wept without exception.

sentences.zh: 黃中乃率其眾復仇，盡殺拜住哥家人及台府官員掾史，獨留拜住哥不殺，以告於張士誠，士誠乃遣其將以兵守紹興。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong then led his host to take revenge, killing all of Baizhuge's family members and the censorate and prefectural officials and clerks. He alone spared Baizhuge, reporting the matter to Zhang Shicheng, who then dispatched his generals with troops to garrison Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong then led his troops in revenge, slaughtering Baizhuge's entire family along with censorate and prefectural officials and clerks. He spared Baizhuge alone and reported the matter to Zhang Shicheng, who dispatched generals to garrison Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 拜住哥尋遷行宣政院使，監察御史真童糾言：「拜住哥陰害帥臣，幾致激變，不法不忠，莫斯為甚。

translations.literal: Baizhuge was soon transferred to commissioner of the Branch Commission for the Spread of Governance. Supervising Censor Zhentong submitted an accusation, saying: "Baizhuge secretly harmed a commanding minister, nearly causing a violent uprising. In lawlessness and disloyalty, nothing exceeds this."
translations.idiomatic: Baizhuge was soon transferred to commissioner of the Branch Commission for the Spread of Governance. Supervising Censor Zhentong impeached him, declaring: "Baizhuge secretly murdered a commanding general, nearly provoking a full-scale revolt. In lawlessness and disloyalty, his crime knows no equal."

sentences.zh: 宜稽諸彝典，置於嚴刑。

translations.literal: He should be judged according to the canonical statutes and subjected to severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He should be judged by the statutes and punished with the utmost severity.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔削拜住哥官職，安置潮州，而邁里古思之冤始白。

translations.literal: "Thereupon an edict stripped Baizhuge of his office and posts and exiled him to Chaozhou, and Mailigusi's wrongful death was at last cleared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then stripped Baizhuge of his rank and exiled him to Chaozhou, and Mailigusi's wrongful death was at last vindicated.
